analysis.category: 角色化 Agent 工作流 / 团队 Prompt 资产

items.title: GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix
items.summary: Netflix 把首页推荐从多阶段召回/排序改造成自回归整页生成：用户上下文是 prompt，行、实体和布局是 token 化 response，再用 WBC/RL 与业务规则约束对齐。线上 A/B 对成熟生产系统取得显著核心参与指标提升，并将端到端 serving latency 降低 20%。

interpretation.businessProblem: 首页不是一条排序列表，而是二维布局：行、实体、顺序和会话反馈互相影响。多阶段 pipeline 容易目标错位、特征工程重、上线迭代慢。
interpretation.systemMechanism: 把用户历史、profile、请求上下文、页面行和实体序列化为领域 token；decoder-only transformer 自回归生成页面，结合 WBC 做 token 价值估计、RL 做页面级 reward、约束解码处理业务规则和冷启动。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 线上看核心参与指标、A/B 显著性、端到端延迟、类别分布漂移和 in-session 响应；离线看 WBC loss、页面 reward、多样性、上下文增量收益和模型规模收益。
interpretation.borrowable: 最值得借鉴的是“领域 token + 整页/整屏 reward + 约束解码 + 多 cadence fresh training”，而不是简单把 LLM 接到推荐链路。
interpretation.boundary: 物料少、页面结构简单、缺少 reward system 或无法承受生成式 serving 治理的团队不宜直接复制。

items.title: SilverTorch: Index as Model — A New Retrieval Paradigm for Recommendation Systems
items.summary: Meta SilverTorch 把传统检索微服务、索引、过滤和粗排统一为 GPU 上的单一神经网络，把“索引”变成模型张量，在 80M item 评估中相对强基线给出 23.7x throughput 和 20.9x TCO efficiency 信号。

interpretation.businessProblem: UGC 推荐需要在 100ms 内从百万级候选缩到千级候选，传统微服务索引限制模型复杂度和候选评估规模。
interpretation.systemMechanism: Index as Model：把相似检索、eligibility filtering、多目标 engagement scoring 和候选返回表达为统一模型模块，让一次请求穿过同一神经检索系统。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 核心指标是 throughput、TCO、sub-100ms 延迟、召回质量、候选覆盖和下游排序收益；必须同时看 GPU 利用率和在线业务指标。
interpretation.borrowable: 对大规模推荐平台，可借鉴“检索组件模型化”和 GPU 批处理统一执行，减少微服务拼接带来的延迟与目标错位。
interpretation.boundary: 候选规模不大、GPU serving 能力不足或业务规则高度离散时，统一模型会增加调试和回滚难度。

items.title: Unlocking dependable responses with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform's Agentic RAG
items.summary: Google Research 的 Agentic RAG 把企业检索改成计划、改写、fanout、充分上下文判定和迭代检索闭环；相对标准 RAG，在 factuality 数据上最高提升 34%，cross-corpus FramesQA 达到 90.1% 正确率且延迟接近单库。

interpretation.businessProblem: 企业知识分散在多个 corpus，单次 RAG 往往只拿到局部证据，复杂多跳问题会误答或过早声明找不到。
interpretation.systemMechanism: Root/Planner/Query Rewriter/Search Fanout/Sufficient Context/Synthesis agents 组成闭环；充分上下文代理明确缺口并触发再次检索。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 看答案正确率、grounding、缺口识别准确率、跨库路由成功率、延迟、引用完整性和人工复核通过率。
interpretation.borrowable: 可把 sufficient-context gate 做成企业搜索/RAG 的上线门禁：没有足够证据就继续搜或拒答。
interpretation.boundary: 低复杂度 FAQ、数据权限不清或没有可审计引用链路时，多 agent RAG 会放大成本和权限风险。

items.title: Meta Adaptive Ranking Model: Bending the Inference Scaling Curve to Serve LLM-Scale Models for Ads
items.summary: Meta 讨论在实时广告推荐中服务 LLM-scale 排序模型的复杂度/效率矛盾，核心是让模型容量、延迟预算和广告业务目标共同优化。

interpretation.businessProblem: 广告候选、排序和竞价需要同时控制转化价值、用户体验、延迟与算力成本，单点模型提升很难直接证明业务收益。
interpretation.systemMechanism: 把用户行为序列、实时上下文、候选生成、轻量排序、精排/重排和预算约束拆成可观测阶段，并在高价值候选上投入更重模型。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 优先看 CTR、CVR、CPA/ROAS、广告质量、P95 延迟、推理成本和预算消耗；在线实验要同时观察广告主价值与用户负反馈。
interpretation.borrowable: 可借鉴分阶段候选裁剪、实时特征注入、模型容量自适应和在线/离线差异诊断，把算力预算变成排序策略的一部分。
interpretation.boundary: 流量小、转化回传慢、成本归因不清或缺少在线实验平台时，不适合直接复制大厂多阶段广告架构。

items.title: From Clicks to Conversions: Architecting Shopping Conversion Candidate Generation at Pinterest

interpretation.businessProblem: 下游转化比点击更能代表广告主价值，但 offsite conversion 稀疏、延迟且噪声大，传统 engagement retrieval 无法稳定优化低漏斗目标。
interpretation.systemMechanism: 跨 Homefeed/Related Pins/Search 合并训练以缓解稀疏，加入 surface-specific features；用 click/repin 补充正样本，用无互动曝光做 harder negatives。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 看 CTR、CVR、RoAS、ad funnel survival、召回覆盖、转化延迟校正和不同 surface 的分桶表现。

interpretation.boundary: 转化回传质量差、广告主规模小或无法做延迟归因时，专用转化召回可能学到噪声。

interpretation.boundary: 没有黄金集、合规边界或评审 rubric 时，LLM 标签会把偏差规模化。

items.title: SABER-Math: Automated Benchmark for Information Retrieval Evaluation in Mathematics
items.summary: As agentic AI systems tackle more complex mathematical tasks, they increasingly rely on information retrieval (IR) to search problem databases, theorem libraries, and educational resources. However, choosing the right retriever remains difficult, as it is infeasible to directly isolate its effect on downstream performance. On the other hand, existing retrieval-specific benchmarks often fail to capture fine-grained mathematical relevance, penalizing relevant documents. We address this gap by introducing SABER-Math, the first fully automated benchmark for evaluating mathematical IR without expert annotation. Starting from 283K high-school-level math problems with solutions, SABER-Math builds challenging reranking tasks in three steps: (i) first, LLMs extract concise solution summaries and mathematical topics for each problem; (ii) then, per-query relevant documents are discovered using ontology topic-based and lexical solutions-summary-based similarities, and (iii) finally, a Swiss-style LLM preference tournament produces fine-grained relevance ratings for the documents. We evaluate lexical retrievers, specialized mathematical retrieval systems, and recent embedding models. We find that while modern embedding models substantially outperform classical and math-specific baselines, even the strongest systems struggle in symbol-heavy domains like Algebra and Calculus. Importantly, we show that general-purpose IR benchmarks such as MTEB do not reliably predict mathematical performance, especially for recent embedding models, highlighting the need for math-specific retrieval benchmarks.

items.title: Scoring Is Not Enough: Addressing Gaps in Utility-fairness Trade-offs for Ranking
items.summary: Scoring functions are used to represent the relevance of individual documents. In modern information retrieval or recommendation systems, they are often learned from data and play a pivotal role in ranking sets of documents or items in a way that maximizes utility to a query or user. With the recent interest in algorithmic fairness, the success of scoring has naturally led to methods that learn scores that simultaneously trade off fairness and utility. In this work, we show that in stark contrast with utility-centric objectives, scoring is sub-optimal in achieving all utility-fairness trade-offs. We establish this with a series of counter-examples with a generic fairness formulation. We show that the issue persists whether we have a deterministic scoring function or a randomized one, or whether we measure fairness at the scope of a single query or across multiple queries. On the positive side, we empirically demonstrate that semi-greedy post-processing has the potential to achieve much better trade-offs, often approaching the ideal of exhaustive post-processing in a tractable way.

items.title: Fast and Feasible: Permutation-based Constrained Reranking for Revenue Maximization
items.summary: Search and recommender systems have produced highly relevant search results. A natural next step in the development of such systems in e-commerce is to rerank these results to increase the platform's revenue from paid promotion products. However, maximizing revenue alone may degrade the user experience by reducing relevance or increasing fraud risk. To avoid this, we state the reranking problem as an integer linear program ($ILP$) that maximizes revenue subject to per-query constraints on other metrics, e.g., relevance. Since solving $ILP$ exactly for every query is slow for deployment to the online service, we propose a lightweight permutation-based reranking approximation algorithm PermR. At each step, the algorithm selects a pair of neighboring items and swaps them to either improve the objective or repair a violated constraint. We evaluate PermR across multiple categories of a large classified platform in offline and online settings. PermR achieves about 63\% of the ILP revenue improvement, within production latency limits, preserving all constraints. In a 14-day online A/B test over 56 million search queries, PermR increased revenue by $2$\%.

items.title: GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix
items.summary: Netflix 把首页推荐从多阶段召回/排序改造成自回归整页生成：用户上下文是 prompt，行、实体和布局是 token 化 response，再用 WBC/RL 与业务规则约束对齐。线上 A/B 对成熟生产系统取得显著核心参与指标提升，并将端到端 serving latency 降低 20%。

interpretation.businessProblem: 首页不是一条排序列表，而是二维布局：行、实体、顺序和会话反馈互相影响。多阶段 pipeline 容易目标错位、特征工程重、上线迭代慢。
interpretation.systemMechanism: 把用户历史、profile、请求上下文、页面行和实体序列化为领域 token；decoder-only transformer 自回归生成页面，结合 WBC 做 token 价值估计、RL 做页面级 reward、约束解码处理业务规则和冷启动。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 线上看核心参与指标、A/B 显著性、端到端延迟、类别分布漂移和 in-session 响应；离线看 WBC loss、页面 reward、多样性、上下文增量收益和模型规模收益。
interpretation.borrowable: 最值得借鉴的是“领域 token + 整页/整屏 reward + 约束解码 + 多 cadence fresh training”，而不是简单把 LLM 接到推荐链路。
interpretation.boundary: 物料少、页面结构简单、缺少 reward system 或无法承受生成式 serving 治理的团队不宜直接复制。

items.title: SilverTorch: Index as Model — A New Retrieval Paradigm for Recommendation Systems
items.summary: Meta SilverTorch 把传统检索微服务、索引、过滤和粗排统一为 GPU 上的单一神经网络，把“索引”变成模型张量，在 80M item 评估中相对强基线给出 23.7x throughput 和 20.9x TCO efficiency 信号。

interpretation.businessProblem: UGC 推荐需要在 100ms 内从百万级候选缩到千级候选，传统微服务索引限制模型复杂度和候选评估规模。
interpretation.systemMechanism: Index as Model：把相似检索、eligibility filtering、多目标 engagement scoring 和候选返回表达为统一模型模块，让一次请求穿过同一神经检索系统。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 核心指标是 throughput、TCO、sub-100ms 延迟、召回质量、候选覆盖和下游排序收益；必须同时看 GPU 利用率和在线业务指标。
interpretation.borrowable: 对大规模推荐平台，可借鉴“检索组件模型化”和 GPU 批处理统一执行，减少微服务拼接带来的延迟与目标错位。
interpretation.boundary: 候选规模不大、GPU serving 能力不足或业务规则高度离散时，统一模型会增加调试和回滚难度。

items.title: Unlocking dependable responses with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform's Agentic RAG

interpretation.boundary: 没有黄金集、合规边界或评审 rubric 时，LLM 标签会把偏差规模化。

items.title: Surface-Form Neural Sparse Retrieval: Robust Fuzzy Matching for Industrial Music Search

interpretation.systemMechanism: 采用 inference-free sparse retrieval、领域 granular subword tokenization 和短 token 约束，让模型学习 surface robustness；离线索引预计算，线上只做轻量 tokenization/IDF。
interpretation.metricsAndExperiment: 关注 recall@10、throughput、query 编码延迟、long-tail 命中、探索效率和反馈闭环稳定 recall。
interpretation.borrowable: 对音乐、商品、地点等高噪声表面文本，可用领域子词和稀疏神经检索替代纯 n-gram fuzzy matching。
interpretation.boundary: 语义查询为主、低延迟索引更新困难或缺少行为反馈闭环时，收益会下降。

items.title: SABER-Math: Automated Benchmark for Information Retrieval Evaluation in Mathematics
items.summary: As agentic AI systems tackle more complex mathematical tasks, they increasingly rely on information retrieval (IR) to search problem databases, theorem libraries, and educational resources. However, choosing the right retriever remains difficult, as it is infeasible to directly isolate its effect on downstream performance. On the other hand, existing retrieval-specific benchmarks often fail to capture fine-grained mathematical relevance, penalizing relevant documents. We address this gap by introducing SABER-Math, the first fully automated benchmark for evaluating mathematical IR without expert annotation. Starting from 283K high-school-level math problems with solutions, SABER-Math builds challenging reranking tasks in three steps: (i) first, LLMs extract concise solution summaries and mathematical topics for each problem; (ii) then, per-query relevant documents are discovered using ontology topic-based and lexical solutions-summary-based similarities, and (iii) finally, a Swiss-style LLM preference tournament produces fine-grained relevance ratings for the documents. We evaluate lexical retrievers, specialized mathematical retrieval systems, and recent embedding models. We find that while modern embedding models substantially outperform classical and math-specific baselines, even the strongest systems struggle in symbol-heavy domains like Algebra and Calculus. Importantly, we show that general-purpose IR benchmarks such as MTEB do not reliably predict mathematical performance, especially for recent embedding models, highlighting the need for math-specific retrieval benchmarks.

items.title: Scoring Is Not Enough: Addressing Gaps in Utility-fairness Trade-offs for Ranking
items.summary: Scoring functions are used to represent the relevance of individual documents. In modern information retrieval or recommendation systems, they are often learned from data and play a pivotal role in ranking sets of documents or items in a way that maximizes utility to a query or user. With the recent interest in algorithmic fairness, the success of scoring has naturally led to methods that learn scores that simultaneously trade off fairness and utility. In this work, we show that in stark contrast with utility-centric objectives, scoring is sub-optimal in achieving all utility-fairness trade-offs. We establish this with a series of counter-examples with a generic fairness formulation. We show that the issue persists whether we have a deterministic scoring function or a randomized one, or whether we measure fairness at the scope of a single query or across multiple queries. On the positive side, we empirically demonstrate that semi-greedy post-processing has the potential to achieve much better trade-offs, often approaching the ideal of exhaustive post-processing in a tractable way.

items.title: Fast and Feasible: Permutation-based Constrained Reranking for Revenue Maximization
items.summary: Search and recommender systems have produced highly relevant search results. A natural next step in the development of such systems in e-commerce is to rerank these results to increase the platform's revenue from paid promotion products. However, maximizing revenue alone may degrade the user experience by reducing relevance or increasing fraud risk. To avoid this, we state the reranking problem as an integer linear program ($ILP$) that maximizes revenue subject to per-query constraints on other metrics, e.g., relevance. Since solving $ILP$ exactly for every query is slow for deployment to the online service, we propose a lightweight permutation-based reranking approximation algorithm PermR. At each step, the algorithm selects a pair of neighboring items and swaps them to either improve the objective or repair a violated constraint. We evaluate PermR across multiple categories of a large classified platform in offline and online settings. PermR achieves about 63\% of the ILP revenue improvement, within production latency limits, preserving all constraints. In a 14-day online A/B test over 56 million search queries, PermR increased revenue by $2$\%.
